_note: WP-ACADEMY-2 comprehension checks. One check per trackable module (M1-M9). Written from the HAB Sales OS Master Curriculum chapters in this directory. 'answer' is the zero-based index of the correct option and is NEVER sent to the browser; grading happens server-side in lib/checks.js.

questions.q: What is the mission of the first 90 seconds of a call or visit?
options: Quote an accurate price as fast as possible
Make a friend, so the customer's nervous system relaxes enough to receive information
Collect the vehicle's year, make and model
Explain every service the shop offers

questions.q: A customer asks, "Do you work on brakes?" What is the HAB relief line?
options: "Sure, we can do that."
"Brakes usually run between $300 and $600."
"You called the right place!"
"Let me transfer you to a technician."

questions.q: Which of these is one of the 5 common mistakes that kill rapport?
options: Answering the price question in the first 30 seconds
Using the customer's name during the greeting
Standing up when the front bell rings
Pausing after the opening line

questions.q: How many times should you use the customer's first name in the first two minutes?
options: Never, it sounds forced
Exactly three times
At least six times
Only once, at the end of the call

questions.q: What is the phone answering standard in the HAB system?
options: Answer whenever the counter is clear
Let it ring so you never sound desperate
Answer before the third ring, with a smile you can hear
Send every first call to voicemail and call back

questions.q: In the HAB system, where does credibility come from?
options: Confident claims like "we're the best shop in town"
What the customer concludes after seeing the evidence: the tour, the techs, the warranty
Offering the lowest price in the area
A long list of services on the website

questions.q: What are the three legs of the Trust Triangle?
options: Speed, price, convenience
Competence, transparency, trustworthiness
Rapport, custody, closing
Warranty, financing, reviews

questions.q: How long should the shop tour take?
options: As long as the customer wants, up to 30 minutes
Under 30 seconds so you do not waste their time
75 to 90 seconds at a walking pace with eye contact
Five minutes minimum to cover everything

questions.q: How does the shop tour end, and why?
options: With a price sheet, to set expectations
With a drink offer, the final reciprocity trigger that makes the customer a guest
With a hard ask for the repair authorization
With a request for a 5-star review

questions.q: What is one of the three hidden sales inside the tour?
options: By the end of the tour the customer has already mentally agreed to the digital inspection
The customer commits to a maintenance package
The customer agrees to pay a diagnostic fee
The customer signs up for the shop newsletter

questions.q: Why is custody the gateway objective of the whole system?
options: Because the shop gets paid a drop-off fee
Because we cannot inspect, educate on, or sell repairs for a car we do not have in our bay
Because it keeps the parking lot full
Because it lets the techs start work without an estimate

questions.q: On an inbound phone inquiry, what comes FIRST, before any education or pricing?
options: A detailed explanation of what the repair involves
A ballpark price range so the customer can budget
The Quick Close on the appointment: "Is now a good time?" then the East-West time choice
Emailing the customer a brochure

questions.q: A customer says "I need new brakes." What is the HAB move?
options: Take the self-diagnosis at face value and quote a brake job
Treat it as a symptom statement and convert it to a documented concern that a certified tech inspects
Tell them they are wrong about their own car
Refer them to a brake specialty shop

questions.q: What is the East-West close?
options: Asking the customer which side of town they live on
Offering two specific appointment times, like "9:15 or 10:45?", so scheduling collapses to a binary choice
Booking the appointment for whenever the customer feels like it
A discount for morning drop-offs

questions.q: What is the boom board rule?
options: No boom board, no bay: no vehicle enters the bay without the concern documented
The boom board is optional for repeat customers
Techs fill out the boom board after the work is done
Boom boards are only for walk-ins

questions.q: Who is the digital vehicle inspection (DVI) really for?
options: The technician, so they know what is wrong
The service manager, for payroll tracking
The customer: it is the X-ray evidence we hand them so recommendations land as fact, not opinion
The insurance company

questions.q: What single question drives the Green / Yellow / Red classification?
options: "How much will this cost to fix?"
"Does it operate within manufacturer specifications?"
"Will the customer pay for this today?"
"How old is the part?"

questions.q: How are the healthy (Green) findings used in the presentation?
options: They are skipped, only problems are worth talking about
The customer is told what is healthy first, which primes the Good-Good-Bad framing
They are saved for the invoice
They are upsold as preventative replacements

questions.q: What is the correct handling of a Yellow finding?
options: Sell it today while the car is on the lift
Ignore it, only Red matters
Document it as a watch item for the next visit or a scheduled-maintenance conversation
Mark it Red so the customer takes it seriously

questions.q: What is the walk-the-bay standard after a DVI is completed?
options: The advisor meets the tech at the vehicle within 15 minutes, listens first, translates, and both confirm the PRS
The tech texts the advisor a one-line summary
The advisor reads the DVI alone and calls the customer
The tech calls the customer directly

M5.title: Build and Strategize: Run the Bases

questions.q: What is the most common real reason a customer says "let me think about it"?
options: The price is genuinely too high
Overwhelm: too many findings presented at once froze their brain
They found a coupon elsewhere
They never intended to fix the car

questions.q: What belongs on 1st base?
options: The most profitable finding on the DVI
Scheduled maintenance items
The customer's original concern, or an immediate safety threat if they came in with no concern
The cheapest item, to build momentum

questions.q: What is kitchen-sinking, and what is the rule about it?
options: Bundling repairs for a discount; it is encouraged
Dumping every finding into one call; never do it, each base is its own call with its own authorization
Presenting only the safety items; it is required
Letting the tech present findings; it is optional

questions.q: What does PRS stand for, and which step do advisors most often skip?
options: Price, Rebate, Savings; advisors skip Rebate
Problem, Risk, Solution; advisors most often skip Risk, the step that creates urgency
Prepare, Review, Sell; advisors skip Review
Photo, Receipt, Signature; advisors skip Photo

questions.q: What is the Short Stop position on the diamond for?
options: Covering the front counter at lunch
Re-opening a missed safety sale with a fresh voice
Handling parts ordering
Calling customers who left five-star reviews

questions.q: How often should you re-engage the customer during a presentation call?
options: Every 60 to 90 seconds, with a micro-question like "Does that make sense so far?"
Only at the very end, to avoid interruptions
Every five minutes
Never: a polished monologue is more professional

questions.q: What must immediately follow the Total Investment number?
options: A long silent pause so the price sinks in
The Coverage (warranty), with no pause in between
A discount offer
The parts and labor breakdown

questions.q: In Good-Good-Bad framing, what comes before the finding?
options: The price, so there are no surprises
A warning about how serious it is
Two pieces of good news that prime the brain into a receptive state
The customer's trade-in value

questions.q: What do you confirm before presenting the findings?
options: That the customer has their credit card ready
That now is a good time to talk and that they were able to view the photos, video or DVI report
That the customer read the shop's Yelp reviews
That the tech has left for the day

questions.q: Why do micro-questions multiply the close rate?
options: They make the call longer, which builds trust
Each small "yes" compounds, so the final authorization is one more small step instead of a big leap
They distract the customer from the price
They give the advisor time to think

questions.q: How many Boss Battles exist in the HAB system?
options: Five
Seven
Eight
Nine

questions.q: When a customer says "the price is too high," what do they actually mean?
options: "I found it cheaper somewhere else"
"I'm not sure this is real value"
"I want a payment plan"
"I am not fixing this car"

questions.q: What is the first universal rule of objection handling?
options: Never argue: acknowledge first, always
Offer a discount immediately
Repeat the price more slowly
Transfer the call to the manager

questions.q: Why do we never pivot to a discount in response to an objection?
options: Because discounts are illegal in most states
Because it trains the customer to objection-shop you forever; pivot to value or risk instead
Because the software cannot process discounts
Because the warranty becomes void

questions.q: In Boss 9 (the second opinion), what is the hard rule for the Short Stop who joins the conversation?
options: Undercut the advisor's price to save the sale
Never contradict what the advisor already told the customer: reinforce first, then problem-solve together
Tell the customer the advisor was too aggressive
Refuse to discuss any cheaper option

questions.q: When does the close actually happen?
options: In the last 30 seconds of the call, with the right one-liner
It starts at hello: the close is the cumulative result of the seven prior steps done right
Only after a discount is offered
When the customer asks for the total

questions.q: Which of these is an assumptive close?
options: "Do you want to think it over?"
"I'll go ahead and get the parts ordered."
"Should I email you the estimate?"
"Is the price okay with you?"

questions.q: "Which direction would you like your vehicle facing when we bring it up?" is which family of close?
options: The choice (binary) close
The urgency close
The logistical close: the brain engages with parking, and the price is silently accepted
The takeaway close

questions.q: How is Authorization Rate calculated, and what is the target?
options: Cars fixed divided by cars inspected, target 50%
Authorized dollars divided by presented dollars across all bases, target at least 75%
Calls answered divided by calls received, target 100%
Reviews received divided by reviews asked, target 80%

questions.q: What is Home Plate?
options: The final invoice review that reinforces value and sets up the next visit
The cash register
The tech's final quality-control lap
The moment the customer pays their deposit

questions.q: What do the four beats of L.A.S.T. stand for, in order?
options: Listen, Apologize, Substitute, Terminate
Listen, Acknowledge, Solve, Thank
Lead, Ask, Sell, Track
Learn, Adjust, Serve, Train

questions.q: What is the most common recovery failure?
options: Thanking the customer too early
Racing to Solve before doing Listen and Acknowledge, which leaves the customer feeling unheard
Listening for too long
Offering too many solutions

questions.q: Why is "I understand, BUT..." a recovery killer?
options: It takes too long to say
The word "but" deletes everything said before it, breaking the Acknowledge beat
Customers prefer the word "however"
It admits fault and creates liability

questions.q: What does the 24-hour recovery window teach?
options: Wait a day so the customer cools off before you respond
Recovery decays fast: the first hour is worth ten of the next day, and after 24 hours a public review is likely
Complaints expire after 24 hours and can be ignored
Refunds must be issued within 24 hours

questions.q: What is the Service Recovery Paradox?
options: Fixing complaints costs more than it earns
A customer whose problem is handled well often becomes MORE loyal than one who never had a problem
Upset customers always leave no matter what you do
Shops should create small problems on purpose to fix them
